chunks: Perform the pilgrimage and the holy visit (Umrah) for God. But if you are prevented, then send an offering that is easy for you. And do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its place. So whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head, then an expiation of fasting or charity or a sacrificial offering. When you are secure, then whoever performs Umrah in conjunction with Hajj, then send an offering that is easy for him. And whoever cannot find [an offering], then a fast of three days during Hajj and seven when you have returned. Those are ten complete [days]. That is for him whose family was not present in the Sacred Mosque. And fear God and know that God is severe in penalty.

key_terms.الْعُمْرَةَ: Minor pilgrimage or holy visit to Mecca
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: To enjoy/perform Umrah followed by Hajj
key_terms.فِدْيَةٌ: Expiation or compensation for missing a ritual duty

ai.seo_question: What are the expiations and fasting requirements for Hajj if one cannot afford a sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This verse, central to Shia jurisprudence, delineates the specific expiations (Kaffarah) for those prevented from completing Hajj or unable to afford the sacrificial animal (Hady) during Umrat al-Tamattu'. It establishes a hierarchical compensation system—prioritizing sacrifice, then fasting, then charity—while emphasizing that these rulings apply specifically to those whose families are not residents of Mecca, reflecting the practical realities of the early Muslim community.
